title: Generic replacement in degrees at least two
statement:
Let $C/k$ be a smooth integral separated
curve over algebraically closed $k$,
and let $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}k(C)\to C$ be its generic point,
with function field $k(C)$.
For every torsion etale sheaf
$F$, the adjunction map induces

$$
H^q(C,F)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ H^q(C,\eta_*\eta^*F)
\qquad(q\geq2)
$$

on cohomology.

proof.text: *The generic point as an inverse limit.* Let $I$ be the nonempty affine opens $U$ of the integral curve $C$, ordered by reverse inclusion, with $j_U:U\to C$. The generic point belongs to every nonempty open. For two such opens $U,V$, their intersection contains the generic point, and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] supplies a nonempty affine $W\subseteq U\cap V$; hence $I$ is directed. The function field $k(C)$ is the stalk $\mathcal O_{C,\eta}=\varinjlim_{U\in I}\mathcal O_C(U)$ [def-sc-function-field], since affine opens are cofinal among neighbourhoods of $\eta$. By the affine clause of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], $\operatorname{Spec}k(C)=\varprojlim_{U\in I}U$ over $C$, with affine transition maps. The curve is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. Fix an affine etale object $W\to C$. It is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; its etale map to the quasi-separated $C$ is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (the etale map is locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism]). To specialize [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-continuity], choose $U_0\in I$, put $X_U=U$ for $U\subseteq U_0$, $F_0=j_{U_0}^{-1}F$, and $W_0=W\times_CU_0$; at each smaller $U$ its $W_U$ is $W\times_CU$, and the inverse-image composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] identifies the pulled-back sheaf with $F|_U$. The lemma's hypothesis on $W_0$ holds by base change: $W_0\to U_0$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] and of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Its two clauses say that a section of $\eta_*\eta^{-1}F$ over $W$ comes from $j_{U*}j_U^{-1}F$ over $W$ for some $U\subseteq U_0$, and a stage section which becomes zero over the generic point becomes zero after shrinking $U$.

proof.text: *The kernel vanishes generically.* Write $\epsilon:F\to E:=\eta_*\eta^{-1}F$ for the adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and $K=\ker\epsilon$. Let $s\in K(V)$ on an etale $V\to C$. Affine opens of $V$ form an etale cover; on each affine $W\subseteq V$, its image $x\in F(W)$ maps to zero under $\epsilon$. Choose any $U_0\in I$. The unit $F\to j_{U_0*}j_{U_0}^{-1}F$ maps $x$ to a stage section whose image in $E(W)$ is zero. By the zero-detection clause of the continuity statement in step 1, it vanishes at a smaller nonempty affine $U\subseteq U_0$. Naturality of the unit with the monomorphism $K\hookrightarrow F$ then makes the unit $K\to j_{U*}j_U^{-1}K$ kill $s|_W$: $j_U^{-1}$ preserves the monomorphism by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$, $j_{U*}$ is left exact [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and the image of the section under that monomorphism is the already-zero section. Thus $K$ has generically vanishing sections in the precise sense of [lem-sc-generic-vanishing-acyclic].

proof.text: *The cokernel vanishes generically.* Put $Q=\operatorname{coker}\epsilon$. For $t\in Q(V)$, the quotient map $E\to Q$ is an epimorphism, hence by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] an etale cover of $V$ admits lifts of $t$ to sections of $E$. Refine that cover by affine etale objects $W$. By the surjectivity clause of continuity in step 1, each lifted section of $E(W)$ comes from a stage $j_{U*}j_U^{-1}F(W)$ for some nonempty affine $U$. Its image in $j_{U*}j_U^{-1}Q(W)$ is zero: the stage section is the unit image of a section of $F$ on $W\times_CU$, and $F\xrightarrow{\epsilon}E\to Q$ is zero. Naturality of the comparison map from the stage to $E$ therefore shows that the unit $Q\to j_{U*}j_U^{-1}Q$ kills $t|_W$. Hence $Q$ also satisfies [lem-sc-generic-vanishing-acyclic]. This uses no unproved claim that $\eta_*\eta^{-1}F$ or $Q$ is torsion.

source.place: ## Proof, cokernel clause; expanded as in Lean WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/Curve/GenericComparison.lean:293-322

proof.text: *Cohomology comparison.* By [lem-sc-generic-vanishing-acyclic], applied separately to $K$ (step 2) and $Q$ (step 3), $H^i(C,K)=H^i(C,Q)=0$ for all $i>0$. Factor $\epsilon$ as $F\twoheadrightarrow I:=\operatorname{im}\epsilon\hookrightarrow E$. The long exact sequences [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] for $0\to K\to F\to I\to0$ and $0\to I\to E\to Q\to0$ show, for each $q\ge2$, that $H^q(F)\to H^q(I)$ is an isomorphism because $H^q(K)=H^{q+1}(K)=0$, and that $H^q(I)\to H^q(E)$ is an isomorphism because $H^{q-1}(Q)=H^q(Q)=0$. Their composite is the map induced by $\epsilon$, as required.
